claims.conclusion: Intrinsic parameters and inter-sensor extrinsics are different model quantities.
claims.limits: Definitions are model-specific; this does not measure an installation.

claims.conclusion: Engineering parameter fitting is distinguished from metrological calibration and adjustment.
claims.limits: A parameter file alone is not a traceability or uncertainty statement.

claims.conclusion: Fresh-data consistency checking alone is narrower than validation for intended use.
claims.limits: Application requirements and reference uncertainty remain necessary.

claims.conclusion: Imaging boresight relates sensor orientations; a shared optical-axis direction leaves image roll undetermined.
claims.limits: The optical-axis observation alone does not define all three rotation degrees of freedom.

claims.conclusion: Mount orientation, estimator initialization and level correction should be distinguished.
claims.limits: Exact firmware/calibration procedures remain system-specific.

claims.conclusion: PX4 recommends controller placement near the center of gravity and configuration of actual orientation.
claims.limits: A documented recommendation does not prove installed performance.

claims.conclusion: Mounting strategy and vibration must be checked against the board and measurements.
claims.limits: No universal isolation material, distance or vibration threshold is supplied.

claims.conclusion: Antenna sky view and any required ground plane are installation questions for its manufacturer.
claims.limits: No universal ground-plane requirement or separation distance is asserted.

claims.conclusion: Load-dependent magnetic interference can have supported compensation; static calibration alone is insufficient evidence.
claims.limits: CompassMot has model/current-monitor limitations; no powered procedure is reproduced.

claims.conclusion: A static extrinsic transform assumes a stable relative sensor relationship.
claims.limits: Moving or flexing assemblies need a suitable time-varying model or mechanical correction.

claims.conclusion: Camera configurations such as optics and image geometry belong with the calibration.
claims.limits: Changed settings need reassessment; known image rescaling is treated separately.

claims.conclusion: Slant range can be converted using geometry when attitude and terrain assumptions are known.
claims.limits: The simple cosine example is restricted to a single beam and flat level ground.

claims.conclusion: PX4 integrated flow fields are angular axis measurements rather than XY displacement.
claims.limits: No raw MAVLink-to-app conversion is claimed.

claims.conclusion: PX4 supports modeled static-pressure position-error compensation with estimator prerequisites.
claims.limits: This is not a generic correction for blocked ports, arbitrary airflow or leaks.

claims.conclusion: A combined GNSS/compass module has separate position and orientation records.
claims.limits: A single mounting arrow does not describe every sensor reference point.

claims.conclusion: Aircraft FRD uses positive forward, right and down axes.
claims.limits: Actual configured sensor/estimator frames still require inspection.

claims.conclusion: ROS body FLU, camera optical RDF, ENU and NED conventions are distinct.
claims.limits: ROS REP 103 permits documented exceptions.

claims.conclusion: Body and navigation frame horizontal directions generally change relative to each other with attitude.
claims.limits: Axis names do not imply coincident frame origins.

claims.conclusion: Units, quaternion ordering, Euler ordering and transform direction must be explicit.
claims.limits: No convention is inferred merely from a rotation field name.

claims.conclusion: The example uses column-vector point coordinates with p_B = R_BC p_C + t_BC.
claims.limits: A coordinate-map convention is specified rather than presumed universal.

claims.conclusion: The inverse translation is -R^T t; its meaning changes with transform direction.
claims.limits: Numerical rigid-transform round-trip check passed.

claims.conclusion: Avoid applying the same physical correction twice across drivers and estimators.
claims.limits: No installed driver or estimator was inspected.

claims.conclusion: The example 120 mm forward, 40 mm right, 80 mm above becomes [0.120,0.040,-0.080] m in FRD.
claims.limits: Hypothetical input; not a firmware preset.

claims.conclusion: ArduPilot documents IMU/center-of-gravity origin conditions.
claims.limits: Exact release/parameter semantics must match the consuming firmware.

claims.conclusion: Physical reference points may differ from housing centers.
claims.limits: Inaccessible origins must retain estimates and measurement uncertainty.

claims.conclusion: GNSS ARP, frequency-dependent PCO and direction-dependent PCV are different.
claims.limits: Mechanical lever-arm measurement does not determine electrical antenna calibration.

claims.conclusion: The image principal point is different from the three-dimensional optical/projection origin.
claims.limits: Pixel units and metric transform units must remain separate.

claims.conclusion: Inertial velocities of rigidly connected points differ by omega cross r.
claims.limits: This is not the derivative of a constant body-coordinate offset; 0.314159 m/s is a calculated example.

claims.conclusion: ArduPilot describes IMU-offset compensation as partial rather than full acceleration compensation.
claims.limits: No conclusion is generalized to all estimators.

claims.conclusion: A one-degree ray error at a perpendicular plane 100 m away gives 1.745506 m lateral offset.
claims.limits: Plane geometry, not a ground-survey accuracy guarantee.

claims.conclusion: Nominal mounting rotation and residual misalignment are different inputs.
claims.limits: Destination definitions must be checked before conversion.

claims.conclusion: A moving gimbal changes the composite body-to-camera transform.
claims.limits: Requires actual joint geometry, conventions and measurement time.

claims.conclusion: A nonzero baseline can produce depth-dependent parallax despite parallel viewing axes.
claims.limits: No universal pixel overlay or stereo rectification is supplied.

claims.conclusion: Image acquisition event and receipt timestamp are different concepts.
claims.limits: Exposure start versus midpoint must be explicitly identified by the recorder.

claims.conclusion: At constant rates, 20 ms corresponds to 0.30 m at 15 m/s or 1.2 degrees at 60 degrees/s.
claims.limits: Separate hypothetical constant-rate cases; no flight observation.

claims.conclusion: A constant fitted shift does not establish clock stability or eliminate arbitrary jitter.
claims.limits: Hardware clock behavior and resets remain acquisition evidence.

claims.conclusion: Rolling-shutter row timing remains even with short exposure.
claims.limits: Camera-specific row timing/readout configuration remains necessary.

claims.conclusion: Target dimensions, flatness, border, inner corners and corner ordering must match the chosen model.
claims.limits: No universal target type or capture count is prescribed.

claims.conclusion: Incorrect target length scale can preserve ideal reprojections while scaling recovered pose translations.
claims.limits: The 20/25 example applies to target-based pinhole pose, not every jointly constrained solver.

claims.conclusion: Informative camera/IMU motion matters more than repeating uninformative observations.
claims.limits: Excitation requirements depend on the estimated model.

claims.conclusion: The analyzed VINS model has specific pure-translation and single-axis extrinsic degeneracies.
claims.limits: Versioned primary research; not a universal theorem for every calibration application.

claims.conclusion: Bias estimation alone is not full IMU intrinsic calibration; selected models may estimate other terms jointly.
claims.limits: The Lab's importer explicitly requires corrected scale and axes.

claims.conclusion: A fixed candidate checked against fresh observations is different from refitting it.
claims.limits: The check still shares modeling assumptions and possible systematic errors.

claims.conclusion: Acceptance criteria, references and uncertainty must be related to intended use.
claims.limits: No universal numerical acceptance threshold is invented.

claims.conclusion: Residuals, repeated-fit spread and full measurement uncertainty are different quantities.
claims.limits: No solver diagnostic is relabeled physical accuracy.

claims.conclusion: The capability summary is pinned to Lab v0.3.0 commit 8db0394 rather than mutable current work.
claims.limits: Read-only source inspection; no app runtime or hardware test performed.

claims.conclusion: Camera/IMU input requires metric fixed-world poses, corrected gyro/specific force, linked intrinsics and mapped capture times.
claims.limits: Operator clock/configuration declarations are not independently authenticated.

claims.conclusion: Optical-flow import assumes normalized axes, a flat normal target, constant window distance and independent planar motion reference.
claims.limits: No automatic raw MAVLink conversion or arbitrary flight-flow calibration.

claims.conclusion: Camera rigs use 2–8 linked cameras and synchronized declared target-corner observations.
claims.limits: Synchronization declarations and numerical checks do not prove hardware synchronization.

claims.conclusion: Exports include representable ROS files and a version-pinned monocular OpenVINS fragment.
claims.limits: Coefficient/representation limits remain; no destination runtime qualification.

claims.conclusion: Physical, bench, timing, flight and application flags remain false.
claims.limits: Passed numerical checks are not silently promoted to physical evidence.

claims.conclusion: Synthetic data retains synthetic provenance.
claims.limits: A content hash establishes identity, not physical acquisition or authenticity.

claims.conclusion: Optical-axis adjustment angles are not aircraft Euler angles or actuator commands.
claims.limits: Convert through actual mount/joint geometry and remeasure.

claims.conclusion: The Orqa edition is separate, and both app licensing/distribution boundaries remain unchanged.
claims.limits: Private source/distribution documentation was inspected; nothing was released.

claims.conclusion: Symptom rows are hypotheses and checks rather than unique causal diagnoses.
claims.limits: Logs and reproducible observations are needed to distinguish alternatives.

claims.conclusion: Remounting affects lever arms; known pure image scaling differs from changes to optics or undocumented modes.
claims.limits: Temperature/impact checks are scoped engineering advice, not an invented universal interval.

claims.conclusion: The worksheet records ARP/model, corner counts, shutter/event timing and separate qualification outcomes.
claims.limits: A blank or completed template does not itself certify a sensor installation.
